messages:
mike: Weekly CobaltPay account check-in. Error rate climbed to 5.1% this morning vs 0.8% baseline. Spike window 2026-03-18 14:10-14:45 UTC. Can SRE give a quick breakdown by 5xx/timeouts/rate-limits + top endpoints?

olga: On it. Quick breakdown for spike window: 5xx 62%, timeouts 28%, rate-limits 10%. Most 5xx are 502/504 coming from model-host pool D.

diego: CobaltPay is still in onboarding payments flow; if we don't stabilize they may push their POC review. Marking renewal-risk watch.

ops-bot: Alerts: account=cobalt_09 triggered "high-error-rate" x2 and "elevated-queue" x1 between 14:05-14:50 UTC. Incident INC-2026-4512 created.

olga: Top failing endpoints (24h): /v1/generate (48%), /v1/embeddings (20%), /v1/chat/completions (18%), /v1/async (6%), /v1/healthcheck (noisy).

mike: Any sign this is customer-side (sdk change) or our infra?

olga: Traces show many long queues before 502s on pool D; also customer enabled high-concurrency batching yesterday per their rollout notes. Likely combined effect.

tara: I messaged their engineering lead asking them to reduce client concurrency and to temporarily cap max_context to 2500 tokens on payment branch.

diego: Immediate mitigations suggested:
- Apply per-project burst cap + soft concurrent cap
- Route heavy /v1/generate traffic to fallback pool E for 20% of requests
- Add KV prefix cache for repeated system prompts

olga: I'll take the caps and canary routing. ETA 45m to push.

mike: Please post a short metrics snapshot after the canary.

ops-bot: Canary rollout logged at 14:35 UTC -> 15% traffic to pool E. Monitoring.

olga: Early signal: canary error-rate 1.4% vs 5.1% baseline after 10m.

diego: Owners:
- olga -> push caps + canary routing (45m)
- tara -> customer comms + request rollback of client batching (15m)
- mike -> update onboarding plan if unresolved (2h)

mike: Thanks team. We'll reconvene in 90m or sooner if incident escalates.
